analysis.title: In Credit, 16 November 2026
key_insights: Presidents Xi, Trump and Putin meet Thursday for a first three-way summit focused on nuclear arms control. The report judges an arms-reduction deal unlikely, with the realistic outcome a commitment to keep talking or a formal three-way strategic-arms dialogue.
New START expired in February, leaving US and Russia unconstrained. Trump wants a three-power framework that includes China. Xi wants recognition as an equal strategic power but not equal caps.

Core government bond markets bear-flattened last week, most notably in the US. October CPI rose 0.4% m/m headline and 0.3% core, both above expectations, and hawkish Fed commentary ended hopes of a near-term pivot.
Market-implied Fed rate expectations for September 2027 rose from 4.3% to 4.7%. The two-year Treasury yield rose 33bps and the 30-year rose 20bps.

The ECB's Nagel called a December rate hike an obvious outcome. The BoJ's Summary of Opinions stressed tightening over being overly cautious. Markets look for December hikes in the US, Europe and Japan.
Brent fell from $98 to an intraweek closing low of $91 and recovered to $96 after Trump said the Iran conflict could end without a formal deal on Iran's nuclear programme.

The 10-year gilt yield rose 11.2bps to 5.335% and the 30-year rose 12.2bps to 5.781%, extending the sell-off after the BoE's 5 November hike. The 10-year breakeven rose 7.9bps to 3.288%, accounting for 71% of the rise in nominal yields.
Markets price a 77% probability of a December BoE hike. UK labour market data and October CPI this week will decide whether that holds.
Gilt auctions were absorbed comfortably. The £1bn January 2056 auction cleared at 5.54% with 3.75x bid-cover, and the £4bn March 2033 auction at 3.52x, stronger than in August.

Higher yields raise collateral requirements for leveraged LDI portfolios, so the report stresses liquidity buffers. Higher nominal yields support funding ratios for partially unhedged pension schemes.

IG credit rallied despite higher rates. Global IG tightened 5bps to 91bps, Euro IG 6bps to 96bps, US IG 4bps to 89bps and Sterling IG 4bps to 92bps. iTraxx Main tightened 3.5bps to 59.2bps and CDX IG 2.7bps to 58.8bps.

Global technology led IG on strong demand for AI-linked issuance. The tension is between supportive technicals (European inflows, primary demand) and rising all-in yields in a rates market with no ceiling yet.
European corporate and financial issuance was €27.7bn, taking November to €74bn. US issuance reached $42.3bn. Borrowers appear to be front-loading ahead of the year-end slowdown.

European financials bank consolidation continued. UniCredit reported record Q3 2026 results and its Commerzbank acquisition received unconditional EU approval. Crédit Agricole proposed merging its Italian operations with Banco BPM.

US high yield spreads tightened about 20bps to +323bps, yield-to-worst 8.30%. The ICE BofA US HY CP Constrained Index fell 0.27%. Yields sit near the 68th percentile of history, which the report says has historically preceded strong returns.

US HY retail funds took a third straight weekly inflow of $1.4bn. HY issuance slowed to three deals totalling $2.3bn. Leveraged loan average price rose $0.07 to $93.99, with loan funds taking in $911m.
European HY returned +0.46% for a second positive week. Single Bs returned +0.81%, CCCs +0.50% and BBs +0.32%. Spreads tightened 24bps to 343bps and yields fell 8bps to 7.10%.
European HY had net inflows of €138m, including the first managed account inflows since late September. Cedacri priced a €1bn two-tranche senior secured deal on 11 November.

European HY earnings were mixed. Playtech raised 2026 EBITDA guidance above €300m. Negative surprises came from SoftBank ($7bn net loss on a $3.7bn equipment write-down), Iceland, Modulaire, Nissan, Skydance and Wepa.

Agency MBS had a soft week, with the Bloomberg US MBS Index returning -184bps, on rate volatility. October existing home sales fell 5.5% to the lowest volume since 2010. The 30-year mortgage rate is 7.21%.
Non-agency MBS spreads were flat to slightly tighter. Year-to-date non-agency issuance is a post-financial crisis record of $239bn, with about $40bn more expected by year-end.

CMBS conduit spreads were unchanged, with year-to-date SASB issuance at $149bn. ABS issuance was $4.9bn across 10 deals. The AAA-to-below-AAA ABS spread was +99bps against a two-year average of +115bps.
The JACI Diversified lost 72bps, 71bps of it from rates. Fitch downgraded SJM Holdings from B+ to B- with a negative outlook on higher leverage and refinancing needs.

New World Development proposed a fully underwritten HKD24.9bn rights issue at HKD0.90, an 81.5% discount to the pre-suspension close of HKD4.87, alongside an amendment extending HKD73.8bn of Target Facilities maturities by two years.
EM debt was relatively resilient. Sovereign and corporate spreads tightened 4bps and 11bps, while returns were -1.04% for sovereigns, -0.46% for corporates and -1.29% for local markets.
Fitch placed Paraguay's BB+ sovereign rating on negative watch after the Ueno Bank collapse and political transition. Paraguayan 10-year bonds returned -1.68% on the week.
Brazil signalled tighter spending controls and more flexibility to freeze expenditure. Hungary and South Africa are expected to hold rates at upcoming meetings.

sector_views.rationale: Consolidation is the dominant theme: UniCredit's record Q3 and unconditional EU approval of its Commerzbank deal, and Crédit Agricole's proposed Italian merger with Banco BPM.
Global technology led IG tightening on strong demand for AI-linked issuance, reversing recent underperformance.

earnings_insights: UniCredit reported record Q3 2026, beating estimates on net income and revenue (reported, per the report).
Playtech raised full-year 2026 EBITDA guidance above €300 million.
SoftBank reported a $7 billion net loss on a $3.7 billion equipment write-down.
Aggreko, B&M, Premier Foods, Asda and Intralot were solid or in line. Iceland, Modulaire, Nissan, Skydance (flat 2027 free cash flow) and Wepa delivered negative surprises.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Above expectations. Price pressures spread across goods and services, ending hopes of a near-term Fed pivot.
Above expectations. Supported hawkish repricing across the US curve.
Debate has shifted to the size and duration of a tightening cycle.
Geopolitical risk premium persists, with Trump comments on a possible Iran conflict end without a formal deal pushing prices lower mid-week.
Up 11.2bps, driven by inflation expectations (71% of the move from breakevens).
UK labour market data and October CPI this week will determine whether it holds.
Weak housing; median price +0.4% y/y at $417,000.

risk_factors: Rates market has not yet found a ceiling, raising all-in IG yields and costs.
Further central bank tightening: December hikes expected from the Fed, ECB, BoJ and BoE.
Leveraged LDI collateral calls from rising gilt yields require adequate liquidity buffers.
Dispersion in HY: the market punishes idiosyncratic earnings misses quickly, and risk appetite is tied to AI-related equity swings.
Paraguay fiscal and reputational cost of the Ueno Bank collapse, plus Fitch's negative watch.
Fragile risk sentiment from the Iran conflict and the geopolitical premium in oil.
charts_described: Chart of the Week shows estimated nuclear warhead stockpiles by country, 1945-2025, with end-point labels of 3,700, 600 and 4,309 (Statista/Federation of American Scientists, as of 12 June 2025).
vol_and_positioning: US HY retail funds took a third consecutive weekly inflow of $1.4bn, and loan funds took $911m.
European HY had net inflows of €138m, including the first managed account inflows since late September.
The report describes the European HY move as a credit compression trade in a risk-on environment (Single Bs and CCCs outperforming BBs).
Rate volatility rose on the CPI print and hawkish Fed talk, hurting agency MBS.
Positioning note: the Global Rates desk reduced modest long duration and returned to neutral.
geopolitical: Xi, Trump and Putin hold a first three-way summit on Thursday, focused on nuclear arms control, with Ukraine, Taiwan and Iran absent from the agenda.
New START expired in February, leaving the US and Russia without arms limits.
Trump said the conflict with Iran could end without a formal deal on Iran's nuclear programme, moving Brent lower.
A Putin decree placed Japan Tobacco International's Russian assets under temporary administration.
Paraguay: Peña removed from the presidency, Alliana appointed, and prosecutors raided Peña's residence in the Ueno Bank case.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong European inflows and primary demand, plus AI-linked issuance demand, drove IG spreads tighter (Global IG -5bps to 91bps).
tension_points.bear_case: Rising all-in yields in a rates market that has not yet found a ceiling raise costs, and hotter CPI and hawkish Fed commentary pushed all-in IG yields higher.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A further sustained rise in rates with no ceiling, as the report frames it as the key tension.
